theme.title: Seven Seconds or Less
theme.subtitle: Phoenix Suns, 2004–05
theme.recap: Steve Nash returned to Phoenix, Mike D'Antoni unleashed a rapid-fire attack, and the Suns transformed into the league's most electric regular-season team.

questions.prompt: How many more regular-season games did the 2004–05 Suns win than the season before?
questions.note: 33 more wins after Nash's arrival transformed the team.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 33-win improvement over the 2003–04 campaign constituted the third-best year-to-year jump in NBA history.

funFacts.text: Phoenix brought Steve Nash back from Dallas on a major free-agent contract.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Suns re-acquired All-Star guard Steve Nash from the Dallas Mavericks

funFacts.text: Mike D'Antoni's attack prioritized quick ball movement, pick-and-rolls and frequent three-pointers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: emphasized rapid ball movement, pick-and-rolls, and high-volume three-point shooting

funFacts.text: A white memorial patch on the Suns' jerseys honored former coach and broadcaster Cotton Fitzsimmons.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: wearing a white patch on their jerseys for the entire season

questions.prompt: What was Steve Nash's assists-per-game average for the 2004–05 Suns?
questions.note: 11.5 assists each night in his first MVP season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nash finished the season averaging 11.5 assists per game

funFacts.text: Nash shot 50.2% from the field and 43.1% from three during the regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: while making 50.2% of his field goals and 43.1% of his three-pointers

funFacts.text: Nash won MVP while Mike D'Antoni took Coach of the Year and Bryan Colangelo Executive of the Year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He ended up winning the MVP award. D'Antoni was awarded Coach of the Year

funFacts.text: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout during the same season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Quentin Richardson won the Three-Point Shootout

questions.prompt: How many road games did Phoenix win during the 2004–05 regular season?
questions.note: 31 road victories—matching the team's home wins.

funFacts.text: Phoenix posted the same 31–10 record at home and on the road.
The Suns were the NBA's youngest top-seeded team since playoff seeding began in 1984, a mark later displaced by Oklahoma City.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: youngest team to earn the 1-seed since seeding began in 1984

funFacts.text: Phoenix swept the Memphis Grizzlies in the opening playoff round.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In the first round of the playoffs, the Suns swept the Memphis Grizzlies in four games

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Amar'e Stoudemire average in the 2005 playoffs?
questions.note: 29.9 points per game across Phoenix's playoff run.

funFacts.text: Stoudemire also averaged 10.7 rebounds during that postseason.
He scored 40 points in the opening game of Phoenix's series against Dallas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: May 9 Dallas W 127–102 Amar'e Stoudemire (40)

funFacts.text: Phoenix's postseason ended in the Western Conference Finals against the eventual champion San Antonio Spurs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Suns lost 4–1 to the 2-seed, and eventual NBA champion, San Antonio Spurs

questions.prompt: How many points did Steve Nash score in the 2005 playoff clincher against Dallas?
questions.context: Phoenix at Dallas · conference semifinals · Game 6
questions.note: 39 points in Phoenix's overtime series-clinching win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 6 May 20 @ Dallas W 130–126 (OT) Steve Nash (39)

funFacts.text: Phoenix eliminated Nash's former Dallas team in six games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: defeated Nash's former team, the Dallas Mavericks, in six games

funFacts.text: The clincher ended in a 130–126 overtime win for Phoenix.
Shawn Marion grabbed 16 rebounds during that same decisive game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Steve Nash (39) Shawn Marion (16) Steve Nash (12)
